title: Majority Element
description:
# Majority Element

Given an integer array `nums` of size `n`, return the majority element.

The majority element is the value that appears more than `floor(n / 2)` times. You may assume that the majority element always exists in the array, so the answer is unique.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [3,2,3]
**Output:** 3
**Explanation:** The value `3` appears twice in an array of length `3`, which is more than `floor(3 / 2)`.

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [2,2,1,1,1,2,2]
**Output:** 2
**Explanation:** The value `2` appears four times in an array of length `7`, which is more than `floor(7 / 2)`.

## Example 3:

**Input:** nums = [6,5,5]
**Output:** 5
**Explanation:** The majority element does not need to be the first value.

## Constraints:

*   `n == nums.length`
*   `1 <= n <= 5 * 10^4`
*   `-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9`
*   The majority element always exists.

examples.description: The majority value appears twice in a length-3 array.
The majority value appears four times in a length-7 array.
The majority element can appear after other values.

tests.description: All values are already the majority
Majority element is not the first value
Majority appears just over half in an alternating pattern
Majority block is surrounded by other values
Minimum constraint value can be the majority
Repeated cancellations still leave the majority candidate

solutions.name: Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm
solutions.description:
## Approach

Maintain a candidate and a counter. When the counter is zero, choose the current value as the new candidate. Matching values increase the counter; different values decrease it.

## Key Insight

The counter represents unmatched votes for the current candidate after canceling pairs of different values. Because the majority element appears more than half the time, all non-majority values can be canceled with majority values and at least one majority vote must remain. Under the problem guarantee, the final candidate is therefore the answer.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: HashMap Counting
solutions.description:
## Approach

Count each value with a hash map and return the first value whose count exceeds `n / 2`. The problem guarantees such a value exists, so the scan can return as soon as the threshold is crossed.

## Key Insight

This is the explicit counting baseline. It is easy to verify, handles negative and large values directly, and is the natural starting point before teaching the cancellation invariant used by Boyer-Moore.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Sorting Median
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sort the array and return the element at index `n / 2`. A value that appears more than half the time must occupy the middle position after sorting.

## Key Insight

After sorting, all copies of any value are contiguous. Since the majority value covers more than half of the array, its contiguous block must cross the median index no matter where the block starts.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log n)
- Space Complexity: O(log n)

solutions.name: Divide and Conquer
solutions.description:
## Approach

Recursively compute a majority candidate for the left half and the right half. If both halves produce the same candidate, return it. Otherwise, count both candidates across the current range and return the one that appears more often.

## Key Insight

If a value is the majority of the whole range, then it must be a majority candidate in at least one half. Counting the two half-candidates is therefore enough to recover the majority for the merged range.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log n)
- Space Complexity: O(log n)
